spec_features.feature_name: 30-turn hard cap on the agentic loop
spec_features.spec_quote: Creates sustained interaction (max 30 turns) in which frustration can compound.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:178 `for turn_idx in range(max_turns):` bounds the agent loop; max_turns defaults to MAX_TURNS_PER_RUN (config.py:14 `MAX_TURNS_PER_RUN: int = 30`). The loop has no body that extends iterations, so it terminates after 30 turns and returns RunResult with stop_reason='max_turns_reached' (harness.py:170,233). This is an enforced bound that actually ends execution.
spec_features.notes: Both quoted spec features refer to the same single mechanism (the 30-turn loop cap). It is a genuine enforced termination, though it is a frustration-prolonging cap rather than a protective early-exit; the only other stop is STOP_PHRASES (subject voluntarily giving up). Note: run_single passes max_turns=args.max_turns which defaults to None (run_experiment.py:55,122), overriding the function default and yielding range(None) unless --max-turns is given; the cap mechanism itself is real and runs with a value.

spec_features.feature_name: 30-turn hard cap as the only interruption
spec_features.spec_quote: the 30-turn hard cap is the only interruptions; even repetitive loops are preserved for the judge.
spec_features.evidence: Same loop bound: harness.py:178 `for turn_idx in range(max_turns)`. No loop-detection or early-protective termination exists; comments explicitly decline to add one: harness.py ~ 'Check repeated failures via tool result to inject a nudge?  No, keep neutral.' and 'If the model rambles without acting for >3 turns, we could stop, but let's let it run to allow degradation measurement.'
spec_features.notes: The cap is enforced, but the surrounding code deliberately removes any softening/monitoring intervention so degradation is preserved for scoring. This is the opposite of welfare protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: let's let it run to allow degradation measurement.
